thread:
jamie: Quick sync — we need to lock the regional handoff constraints & KPIs for the Q3 onramp. Customers are asking for deterministic region routing + tenant isolation, but infra calls out capacity, egress, and cost constraints. I sketched a launch rubric and a 3-phase onramp. Sharing below — please react with :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown: and any hard constraints we should surface to sales/solutions.
ana: copying infra notes: we can't promise hard affinity without capacity reservations. per-region GPU pools + reserved egress will need contractual commitments. Also: cross-region KV replication increases cost + write latency.
mira: ops view: runbook must include fail-open vs fail-closed behavior. If region is overloaded we need an explicit degradation ladder and automated alerts. Also need an evacuation window and migration coordinator playbook.
sam: arch note: routing policy design options: (1) strict region-affinity (sticky route) (2) best-effort locality with priority tiers (3) region-tagging + fallback model variants. Tier 2 lets us avoid full isolation while satisfying most customers.
jamie: Proposed phased plan (short):
- Pilot (4 wks): 2 pilot customers (one US-west, one EU-west), dedicated slices, manual cutovers, close monitoring.
- Beta (8 wks): open to limited customers, automated routing + simple canary rollouts, cost telemetry turned on.
- GA: full onramp with self-serve tenancy + SLA table.

Launch criteria (proposed, must be measurable):
- Latency: region-local P95 <= 100ms for generation requests for 90% of pilot traffic.
- Fallback: cross-region P95 <= 200ms (for allowed fallbacks).
- Isolation: tenant blast-radius test — one tenant misbehaving should not increase other tenants' error rate by >0.5%.
- Capacity: autoscaling ramp test — able to handle 3x baseline QPS without OOMs.
- Cost delta: per-customer token-unit cost increase <= 20% vs baseline (or show clear tradeoffs).
- Security/compliance: audit log streaming + KMS integration tested.
- Observability: route-level latency/cost dashboards + alerting in Console.
- Rollback: tested rollback policy for routing changes (manual and automated).

ana: constraints to surface to customer teams: egress pricing bands, minimum reserved qps for strict affinity. If they want no cross-region fallback we need a signed commitment for reserved capacity (monthly).

mira: also add a stress test for KV-cache cold starts and quantized model tails. We saw cascades when caches warmed poorly. Recommend we include a cache-warm plan in pilot.

sam: idea — offer 2 product SKUs: "Regional Affinity (soft)" and "Regional Isolation (hard)". Soft gives best-effort locality with cheaper pricing; hard guarantees affinity but with reservation and higher price. Simplifies sales asks.

jamie: decision needed by EOD Friday: prioritization of Pilot customers and whether to accept "no-fallback" asks for pilot. If we accept no-fallback, infra will flag higher commit. Also need to pick owner for migration coordination (PM + Solutions).

ana: I'm available to scope infra work. Short list of blocker items: dedicated pool sizing, egress policy config, KMS end-to-end.

mira: SRE to own runbooks + escalation. I can draft the initial evacuation and degrade playbook — will post in #eng-oncall.

sam: I'll draft a simple routing-policy DSL example we can use in the RFC. Something like:
```
route_policy: 
  - match: tenant.metadata.region == "eu-west"
    action: prefer_local
    fallback: allow_remote
    reserve_qps: 200
```

ops-bot: reminder: please add this thread to the Platform RFC board and tag with `onramp` and `regional-affinity`. Due date set to 2026-07-10.
jamie: Thanks — if no strong objections I'll finalize the rubric + send to sales/solutions by Friday. Add your redlines here.

ana: :thumbsup: will add infra numbers by Thursday.

mira: adding :eyes: and will post runbook draft tomorrow.

sam: will upload DSL sketch and cost model by Thursday.

jamie: great — final note: let's keep the pilot conservative (soft-affinity with opt-in hard isolation) unless customers sign reserved capacity. Keeps risk down.
